newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan ex-rebels slam gov't economic policies.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan ex-rebels slam gov't economic policies.

text.p: Former rebel commanders on Tuesday slammed the Guatemalan government's economic policies for allegedly violating the spirit of a peace treaty ending 36 years of war.

"The economic policies being pushed (by the government) are more and more in contradiction with the spirit of the accords and compromise the country's future," said the faxed statement from the Mexico City offices of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG).
The government of Guatemalan President Alvaro Arzu and the URNG signed a historic treaty on Dec. 29 ending Central America's longest-running and last armed conflict.
The treaty put into effect 11 separate accords on human rights, Indian rights, guerrilla disarmament, reductions in the powerful army, education and social development.
Since the signing, the four URNG leaders who spent most of their lives leading an armed revolt against the government have refrained from criticising Arzu or his policies.
Right-wing business groups and left-wing human rights organisations have criticised the government and the URNG for their mutual kid-gloves treatment.

But the honeymoon appears to be over as the statement criticises the government's free-market economic policies, health code, utility price hikes, privatisation plans, and lifting of price ceilings on basic food products.

The URNG was converting from a military organisation to a legitimate political party. More than 3,000 former guerrillas are living temporarily in demobilization camps where they will turn in arms by May 3.
On Wednesday, Arzu was expected to tout government compliance with the peace accords during the first phase of the peace process.
